title: Luceras Torso
heading: Luceras: the torso
lede: Stage 5 of 11, part 2 of 5. The trunk refined on the approved head build: spine line, chest and keel, shoulder plates, rib cage, belly tuck, loin, hip points, rump. Judge shape only: does the trunk read as the shaved clay body under the fur? Muscle relief is surface work the fur covers; the belly tuck finishes when the hind legs (part 3) move the thigh seam. Approve, or say what needs work and in which view. Confirm notifies the orchestrator.
fallback: Approvals cannot be saved from this view; reply in chat.
compositeEmpty: Confirm closes the torso; the hind legs and feet start next.
confirmed: Torso confirmed; the orchestrator files it and starts the hind legs. Tell the orchestrator you confirmed.

fold.title: Decided by the pipeline owner
fold.text: Both streams got the same brief on the approved head file (B-rv4f), 60-minute cap, Blender queued through the machine lock. Both found the blockout trunk already is the body reconstruction (within 1 mm), so neither ran another reconstruction; the work was brushing the shaved landmarks against your clay views. The Claude pass (B-ej6s, Opus builder) is presented: its landmarks read. The Codex pass (B-eccr) respected every hold but changed so little it is indistinguishable from the base; it is in section 2 for comparison. Both left out a stray review copy of the head that the head file carried; it will be stripped from the base before part 3. Every vertex of the approved head and neck, and of the limbs and tail below their joints, is unmoved in both (measured zero). Costs: Claude 29 minutes wall, about 300K tokens; Codex 17 minutes, 112K tokens.

claude.name: Torso, Claude stream (pass 1)
claude.question: Does the trunk read as the shaved clay body?
judge: Side: chest, back line, belly tuck into the loin, rump as the clay?
Three-quarter: shoulder plate and its back edge, flank, hip points?
Front: chest between the forelegs, shoulder width?
claude.note: Declared for later parts: the belly tuck meets the frozen thigh front lower than the clay (part 3 moves the thigh seam); the hindquarters look wide from the front because of the thighs (part 3); chest depth kept at the approved stage 4 proportion; the trunk is softer than the clay's muscle relief, which the fur covers.
